events.excerpt: GLP-1 medications are everywhere these days. The peptide-based drugs are both highly effective and wildly popular for diabetes, weight loss and a growing range of connected chronic health conditions, including cardiovascular disease and obstructive sleep apnea. But, amid the boom, the latest data suggests millions of Americans have turned to unapproved versions and are using the potent drugs in ways doctors never intended, raising questions about what that real-world use means for safety and efficacy. In a study published this week , researchers at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention broke down survey data of GLP-1 use collected between July and August of 2025. Based on responses from over 8,000 US adults, the researchers estimate that about one in 10 US adults (9.8 percent) used a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, aka GLP-1 medication, in 2025. That's around 27 million adults. The study was published in the CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. Among GLP-1 users, nearly half (44 percent) reported using their GLP-1 in a way that was different from how it was prescribed. This proposal argues that it can be something larger: the first public network able to protect records themselves, not only payments. Zcash Shielded Assets would let anyone issue an asset whose holdings and transfers are private while its total supply stays publicly provable. The specifications exist as drafts, but they are written for the Orchard pool, which no longer accepts new value, and they are not scheduled for any network upgrade. events.excerpt: v2.11.1 is a security and stability release on top of v2.11.0 . It's the public release of v2.11.1-priv , which most validators already run. No hardfork, no config change, no database schema change, no resync required. Nodes can be upgraded one at a time, in any order. Highlights Stateless import : each block's header, and its body against the header, are checked before the block is executed. This applies to both the sequential and the parallel import path. Parallel import waits for a batch's header checks before it executes the batch. Execution and RPC : on a chain with no blob schedule, transaction pre-checks return ErrNoBlobBaseFee ( blob base fee unavailable ) for blob transactions. Operator notes Operators on v2.11.1-priv : same code, switch to v2.11.1 at your next maintenance window. Operators on v2.11.0 : upgrade. All operators should run this release. eth_simulateV1 calls that carry blob hashes return blob base fee unavailable unless the call overrides the blob base fee ( blockOverrides.blobBaseFee ). eth_call , eth_estimateGas and the tracers are unchanged. What's Changed v2.11.1 candidate by @cffls in #2543 Full Changelog : v2.11.0...v2.11.1

events.excerpt: Depending on which type of electric toothbrush you are using, the replaceable brushes may contain an NFC chip that the handle and possibly base station uses to track various details, such as time spent brushing and when to replace the brush. The Philips Sonicare of [Circuit Helper] is one such unit, with its NFC chip tracking aspects like runtime and pressure . Unsurprisingly it’s easy enough to read and write this same NFC chip with a PN532 NFC reader and ESP32-S3 MCU. This reveals data fields for everything from brush type, to total runtime and expected lifetime, inviting a bit of experimentation on how certain usage patterns affects these data fields. This much is perhaps not too shocking, but the fun part is what you can do with the chip after you have figured out how to write to its memory. How to unlock these units and their NXP NTAG213 IC has been figured out a few years ago already, so the hardest part was to figure out what to do with this information. The demonstrated use case in the video is to unlock an Apple Macbook, which is maybe a bit too niche. Also demonstrated is taking the chip and its antenna out of the brush, which turns out to be quite easy. events.headline: Using a Toothbrush’s NFC chip to Unlock a Computer

events.excerpt: Chalk up a new record for vulns. The number of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) found and disclosed so far in 2026 surpassed 100,000 on Friday - more than double 2025’s total - and the reason can be summed up in two letters: AI. “It’s kind of wild,” Josh Bressers, VulnCheck’s director of coordinated vulnerability disclosure, told The Register . “The thing that almost scares the bejesus out of me is while 100K sounds like a lot, in a couple years we're going to say, remember when it was only 100K?” As of the time of our interview, about 4 pm UTC on Friday, VulnCheck counted 100,222 CVEs, he said. Microsoft alone added 1,094 security flaws to the total count on Tuesday, following 1,474 vulnerabilities the month before. “There's no denying the fact that vulnerability hunting with AI is driving a majority of what we're seeing.” All the major CVE Numbering Authorities (CNAs) - these are the organizations authorized by the CVE program to assign unique identifiers to security vulnerabilities - like VulnCheck, Microsoft, Oracle, GitHub, and other large enterprise IT vendors “are just screaming into the atmosphere right now,” Bressers said. “It’s AI.” Meanwhile, the percentage of these bugs that are exploited in the wild remains relatively consistent. events.excerpt: The internet is full of schlock, from biased news and dubious hot takes to false factoids. LogicLens aims to separate fact from fiction using the very same technology behind some of that slop: AI. It’s a simple premise, really: LogicLens, which lives in Chrome as a browser extension , or on iOS in the form of a mobile app called Receipts , combs through articles, social media posts, and other content to check it not only for factual inaccuracies, but also for bad reasoning. LogicLens and Receipts claim to identify logical fallacies , flag reports that misrepresent information, detect content that attempts to polarize an issue, and the like. It also cites sources, so if, for example, you need to call someone out on their BS, you’ll have ammunition. Or, if you’re trying to fact-check something before sharing it, you can get a more accurate view of the situation, and maybe post something else instead. Using the Chrome extension is as simple as clicking on its icon in the list of extensions in the browser. On iOS, the Receipts app is found as a share option. Once it starts, LogicLens scans an article, post, video, etc. to find potential issues of factual or logical inconsistency and flags them for review. events.excerpt: We introduced Kitesurf , our stateless browser for AI agents that runs entirely on top of Workers, in August and followed up in September with WebMCP support, new APIs, and improved compatibility. On every occasion, we mentioned our commitment to open sourcing it so that developers could run their own browser engine on their own Cloudflare accounts if they want to. That promise is now real. Kitesurf is open source on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 license. You can read the code, run it locally, change it, and deploy your own instance to Cloudflare Workers. A browser built for agents Kitesurf runs entirely on Cloudflare Workers. It parses HTML, applies CSS, executes page JavaScript, and renders screenshots without a browser container. It supports the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP), so you can connect clients such as Puppeteer. Our main goal is to give AI agents a lightweight, efficient browser — one that can load websites, execute JavaScript, and interact with pages while using less CPU and memory than a full browser like Chromium, and scaling on demand across Cloudflare’s global Workers network. Read more about why and how we built Kitesurf in our initial announcement and how to use it in Browser Run’s developer documentation. What is inside the repository? Kitesurf builds on Cloudf
events.headline: Kitesurf is now open source
